spec.description: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 water-risk indicators for the 6,500 river-basin units of South America, read live from ArcGIS Online: choose an indicator and the countries, compare countries, list the worst basins, and draw an area on the map to narrow the counts, the ranking and the table.

options.content:
# Water risk — WRI Aqueduct 4.0

The polygons are **HydroBASINS level 6 basins cut by province**, served live from the ArcGIS Online Feature Service, **with no prior download and no ETL**. Changing the indicator queries the service again; picking countries (in the selector or by clicking the bars of the ranking) filters the map in the browser.

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | [Aqueduct 4.0 Water Risk](https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=c784f4ebddaf43c8b816612fb62e7e5b) · **Aqueduct 4.0, World Resources Institute (WRI)**, hosted by Esri. Licensed CC BY 4.0 |
| Coverage | 13 countries of South America · 6,469 units with data for water stress (out of 6,717) |
| How it arrives | Infinity → `f=geojson` → a `geojson` column → the panel detects it and kepler draws it |

**Three things to know so as not to misread the map:**

- **The gaps are "No Data".** Aqueduct encodes a missing value as `-9999`, and a single `-9999` would
  wreck the colour scale, so they are filtered at source (`$​{indicador}_score >= 0`). What is missing
  from the map is data that does not exist, not zero risk.
- **"Arid and Low Water Use" scores high by convention**, not from measured stress: these are 493 arid
  units with little water use. They come out red without there being any competition for the resource.
- **Level 6 is coarse.** It works for a national or regional read. It does not work at municipal scale.

**Filtering by drawing on the map.** With the map's draw tool (polygon or rectangle) you can narrow the
analysis: the ranking by country, the table and the "In selection" counter come to describe only the
basins the shape touches. **The map deliberately does not filter itself** — it goes on showing the whole
extent as context, because if its own query depended on the shape, shrinking the dataset would leave no
way to widen it again from the map. To go back to the total, delete the shape.

spec.description: Left: the authoritative count over the whole extent, computed by ArcGIS without paging — it is the contrast that gives away a pagination truncation on the map. Right: what the drawn polygon encloses. With no shape, they agree.
spec.title: Units

spec.description: Mean score per country of the units the drawn area touches (all of them with no area), aggregated on the ArcGIS server: one request, ~2 KB, no pagination. Each bar has the colour the map gives a basin with that score. **Click a bar** to filter the map, the counter and the table by that country; more clicks add countries, a picked one clicked again leaves (the last one out means all). The map filters in the browser, with no new request; the countries not picked stay here in grey.
